content.content:
Empowering Women with SCAD or ANOCA through Citizen Science

The EMPOWER-BP study uses wearable blood pressure monitoring and citizen science to engage women with SCAD or ANOCA directly in their health management.

block1.title: About EMPOWER-BP
block1.content:
The **EMPOWER-BP** study (Empowering Women with SCAD or ANOCA through Citizen Science: Evaluating the Efficacy of Huawei's Blood Pressure Monitoring Watch) is a clinical study within the **EXIT-CVD** research consortium, co-funded by the **European Union Innovative Health Initiative (IHI)**.
Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection (SCAD) and Angina with Non-Obstructive Coronary Arteries (ANOCA) are cardiovascular conditions predominantly affecting women, yet remain significantly underdiagnosed and undertreated. EMPOWER-BP uses wearable technology and citizen science to engage patients directly in their health management.

block2.title: Study at a Glance
block2.content:
| | |
|---|---|
| **100** Participants | **Citizen Science** Approach |
| **12 months** Monitoring | **Observational** Study |

Led by **UMC Utrecht**, with support from Vrouwenhart Professionals and the RADAR-base platform at King's College London.

blocks.title: Powered by Onsentia & RADAR-base
blocks.content:
Onsentia powers the digital data collection and remote monitoring infrastructure for the EMPOWER-BP study using the open-source **RADAR-base** platform.
The platform combines: - **Active monitoring (aRMT)** — Patient-reported outcome questionnaires (monthly eCRF completion) - **Passive monitoring (pRMT)** — Sensor and wearable data collection - **Huawei BP Watch** — Continuous blood pressure monitoring Data is collected digitally via the RADAR platform, adhering to GDPR standards, with secure transmission and storage at UMC Utrecht.

content.title: Study Objectives
content.content:
**Primary:** Assess feasibility and adherence to continuous BP monitoring using Huawei's watch among women with SCAD and/or ANOCA.

**Secondary:** Evaluate correlation between BP patterns and symptom recurrence, determine changes in clinical management, assess patient engagement and quality of life, and conduct health economic analysis.

content.title: Part of EXIT-CVD
content.content: EMPOWER-BP is one of the "early exit" studies within the **EXIT-CVD** consortium, which brings together 42 partners across 17 countries to transform how cardiovascular disease is detected, monitored and treated across Europe.

blocks.title: Why This Matters
blocks.content:
SCAD and ANOCA are cardiovascular conditions predominantly affecting women, yet remain significantly underdiagnosed due to atypical presentation and diagnostic challenges. Continuous, non-invasive blood pressure monitoring may help in early detection of symptom recurrence and better management of these conditions.
By leveraging citizen science and social media communities, EMPOWER-BP aims to overcome recruitment challenges, improve patient engagement, and enhance long-term adherence to monitoring — empowering women to take an active role in managing their cardiovascular health.

items.title: 1. Check eligibility and provide consent
items.content: Complete a brief eligibility check, read the Participant Information Sheet, and sign an electronic consent form.

items.title: 2. Set up your study account
items.content: Create an account with your email and a password. Verify your email to proceed.

items.title: 3. Connect your devices
items.content: Connect the Huawei BP Watch, install the RADAR Active App (aRMT) for questionnaires, and the RADAR Passive App (pRMT) for passive data collection.

items.title: 4. Participate in monitoring
items.content: Wear the Huawei BP Watch as instructed for continuous blood pressure monitoring, complete monthly questionnaires via the Active App, and attend quarterly virtual check-ins. The study lasts 12 months.
